spec_features.spec_quote: Default `max_turns = 12`, tasks may override up to 14.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:96 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns):` enforces the turn cap and ends the loop; runner.py:82 `max_turns = task.get('max_turns', args.turn_limit)`; manifest.yaml sets max_turns 12/14. The cap is genuinely enforced and bounds execution. However the 'override up to 14' ceiling is NOT enforced anywhere — no clamp/min() limits the override (grep shows no cap check), so a manifest could set any value; the '14' is merely the values chosen in the manifest.
spec_features.notes: Turn cap runs and breaks the loop, but the claimed 14-turn ceiling is not enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: --turn-limit ... help="Max turns per trial" (runner.py); no welfare comment

spec_features.evidence: finish is a real tool (loop.py:38-50), dispatched in run_tool (loop.py:74-75), and honored as a stop: when called it sets `finished = True` (loop.py:126-127) and the loop breaks on the next iteration (`if finished: break`, loop.py:97-98). End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: Stop is honored at the top of the next iteration (before the next model call), not mid-turn, but it does halt the session.

spec_features.evidence: The only code path that sets `finished`/breaks early is the finish branch (loop.py:126-127); no other tool or condition exits early. submit_code never breaks. The system prompt also offers it when 'stuck' (loop.py:18).
spec_features.notes: Accurately the sole early-exit mechanism and it works.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "You may call finish when you are done or stuck." (loop.py:18)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** stop on repeated identical failures.
spec_features.evidence: This describes the deliberate ABSENCE of a protective stop. Confirmed: nothing in loop.py monitors repeated/identical failures or breaks on them — the loop only breaks on `finished` (loop.py:97-98) or exhausting `range(max_turns)`. No welfare-protective halt exists. The judge merely records repetition/tool-misuse scores post-hoc (judge.py) but never feeds back into the loop.
spec_features.notes: Anti-welfare design choice; no protection implemented.

code_only_features.evidence: models.py:61 and models.py:104 pass `max_tokens=800` to both OpenAI and Anthropic API calls, enforcing a per-turn output ceiling. It is actually sent to the API and bounds generated output.
